column4: Manual repayments - Change the way how the Redemption fee is applied
column7: 5.3. - Update repayment distribution, Redemption fee update, Top-ups/Consolidations for the Customers/Agents
column18:
# Currently, the system applies a Redemption fee during Manual repayment in case when the cumpayment_actual is bigger than cumpayment_expected by more than 2 monthly repayments
# The system shall not charge the Redemption fee if the Manual repayment amount is <= 2*Net Monthly repayment within 1 month  
# If the Value date of a newly created Manual repayment transaction is before the Value date of the existing transaction within the same loan, the system shall redistribute the money of the existing transactions accordingly

*Example 1:* 

# Net Montly repayment = $200
# cumpayment_expected = $10,000
# cumpayment_actual = $11,500
# Value date of the Manual repayment (Transaction A) = 07.01.2025
# Manual repayment amount = $270
# Other repayments in January 2025: 
## Transaction B = $50 (03.01.2025)
## Transaction C = $100 (05.01.2025)
# Redemption fee is calculated from the $20 ($50 + $100 + $270 - 2*$200 = $420 - $400 = $20)

*Example 2:*

# Net Montly repayment = $200
# cumpayment_expected = $10,000
# cumpayment_actual = $11,500
# Value date of the Manual repayment (Transaction A) = 07.01.2025
# Manual repayment amount = $270
# Other repayments in January 2025: 
## Transaction B = $50 (03.01.2025)
## Transaction C = $100 (16.01.2025)
# In this scenario, the Value date of a new transaction is before the Value date of the existing transaction ($100 (16.01.2025)). So, the system shall redistribute the money from every transaction that goes after 07.01.2025:
## Redemption fee for Transaction A: $50 + $270 = $320. Since $320 < 2*Net monthly repayment ($400), on 07.01.2025 the limit wasn’t exceeded, and therefore the Redemption fee = 0
## Redemption fee for Transaction C: $320 + $100 = $420. Since $420 > 2*Net monthly repayment ($400), on 16.01.2025 the limit was exceeded by $20, and the Redemption fee will be calculated out of this $20. 



*IMPORTANT!!!* 

There could be a case when the Manual repayment transaction will be placed before the Batch file repayment transaction (Transaction C is a Batch file repayment). In this case, the system shall not apply the Redemption fee to the Batch file repayment transaction since it is not allowed by the business rules. 

In this scenario, the system shall just redistribute the money from the Batch file repayment transaction among Principal/Interest/Fees.

h3. Summary

The issue involves a problem with the first payment date for a new loan when a customer tops up their loan after making an early payment on the old loan. The new loan's first payment date is incorrectly set to the calendar due date, causing it to appear in arrears.

h3. Context

* *Feature:* Loan Top-Up (Payday). See [business rules documentation|docs/features/easypayday/loan-management/loan-management/05-business-rules.md].
* *Current behaviour:* The system uses the upcoming payment date based on the calendar for calculations. The required behaviour is to use the first unpaid instalment date instead, with a safeguard for the disbursement date.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* The system must calculate the first instalment date using the first unpaid instalment from the existing loan’s payment schedule, based on the current principal balance at top-up.
* When creating the top-up application, the new loan’s first payment date must follow the same logic of using the first unpaid instalment.
* If the first unpaid instalment date is before the top-up disbursement date, the system should use the first schedule date on or after the disbursement date.
* The first instalment date must remain read-only in the top-up UI, with no new user inputs allowed.
* Existing top-up eligibility, validation, and disbursement-date rules must remain unchanged.
